state.name: South Carolina
state.agency: South Carolina Department of Natural Resources
state.peak_intrusion_season: March through May for spring raccoon and squirrel denning and bat maternity colonies forming, summer for armadillo digging, skunk grubbing, and snake activity across the Lowcountry, and September through November as rodents and squirrels seek winter shelter — with the Lowcountry staying active far later into the year than the Upstate
state.climate_factor: South Carolina's humid subtropical climate keeps snakes, armadillos, and bats active late into fall on the coast and brings them back early in spring, hurricane and king-tide flooding from June through November pushes marsh and swamp animals into Lowcountry neighborhoods, and even Upstate winters are mild enough that attic pressure never fully stops
state.permit_note: South Carolina has no nuisance wildlife control operator license — SCDNR lists wildlife control operators by county as a referral service and states plainly that it in no way endorses or guarantees the services of any operator on that list. The authority for the work is the free depredation permit SCDNR issues under S.C. Code Section 50-11-2570 (valid 30 days, one year for beaver), hunting and commercial fur licenses for in-season trapping, and the codified homeowner rule in Section 50-11-2570(B) covering furbearers and squirrels captured within 100 yards of a home that is being damaged — an animal captured under that rule must be destroyed or, with a department permit, may be relocated. Routine relocation of wildlife is against state law in South Carolina, and no permit at all is required to remove bats, though SCDNR guidance on timing still applies

Abbeville County.region: the western Piedmont on the Savannah River, along the South Carolina-Georgia line
natural_features: Richard B. Russell Lake on the Savannah River
Long Cane Creek and the Long Cane Ranger District of Sumter National Forest
the historic Abbeville town square
Abbeville County.habitat_type: rolling Piedmont farmland and pine-hardwood forest broken by Sumter National Forest tracts and the Russell Lake shoreline
Abbeville County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums work the Russell Lake shoreline and Long Cane Creek bottoms into lake and farm homes, armadillos root pastures and lawns across the county, and bats hold colonies in Abbeville's older in-town houses
Abbeville County.absent_or_rare: alligators and cottonmouths are not part of this Piedmont county's working list, and groundhogs thin out toward its southern edge, though both stay matters of identification rather than routine calls

Aiken County.region: the western Midlands Sandhills on the Savannah River, across from Augusta, Georgia
Aiken County.nearest_metro: Augusta, Georgia (directly across the Savannah River)
natural_features: the Savannah River and its swamp bottoms
Hitchcock Woods, one of the largest urban forests in the country
the Aiken Gopher Tortoise Heritage Preserve and the Sandhills longleaf country
Aiken County.habitat_type: Sandhills longleaf pine and turkey oak over deep sand, giving way to Savannah River swamp and horse-country estates around Aiken
Aiken County.regional_wildlife: armadillos are a routine lawn and burrow call across the Sandhills sand, raccoons and squirrels work the Hitchcock Woods edge straight into Aiken attics, and the Savannah River bottoms hold opossums, skunks, and cottonmouths along the wet ground
Aiken County.absent_or_rare: the gopher tortoise and its burrows in the Sandhills are State Endangered and referral-only through SCDNR, and the southern hognose snake of these sandhills is State Threatened and never a removal job

Allendale County.region: the western Lowcountry along the Savannah River, in the state's least populated corner
Allendale County.nearest_metro: Augusta, Georgia (about 55 miles northwest) and Savannah, Georgia (about 70 miles southeast)
natural_features: the Savannah River and its floodplain swamps
the Lower Savannah River bottomland hardwoods
Red Bluff and the county's creek swamps
Allendale County.habitat_type: flat Lowcountry farm and timber land over Savannah River floodplain swamp, creek bottoms, and pine flatwoods
common_wildlife: feral hogs in the river swamp
Allendale County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, opossums, and armadillos work the river swamp and creek bottoms into the county's small towns, feral hogs root the floodplain fields, and alligator sightings belong to the Savannah River backwaters
Allendale County.absent_or_rare: groundhogs are scarce this far into the Lowcountry, and alligators here are an SCDNR tag-and-agent matter, never a private removal service

Anderson County.region: the Upstate foothills between Greenville and the Georgia line, on Lake Hartwell
natural_features: Lake Hartwell and its many creek arms
the Saluda River headwaters
Sadlers Creek and the county's foothill hardwood ridges
Anderson County.habitat_type: Upstate foothill suburbs and small cities giving way to pasture, hardwood ridges, and the Hartwell lakeshore
Anderson County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow pasture edges and subdivision banks across the foothills, raccoons and squirrels work the Hartwell creek arms into lake and suburban homes, and armadillos have spread into the county's southern lawns
Anderson County.absent_or_rare: cottonmouths do not reach this Upstate county, and copperheads in the rocky foothill woods are identification-and-safety calls, not removal promises

Bamberg County.region: the inland Lowcountry on the South Fork of the Edisto River
Bamberg County.nearest_metro: Orangeburg (about 20 miles north) and Charleston (about 75 miles southeast)
natural_features: the South Fork Edisto River and its blackwater swamps
the county's Carolina bays and creek bottoms
pine flatwoods and farm fields across the inner Coastal Plain
Bamberg County.habitat_type: inner Coastal Plain farm and timber land threaded by blackwater Edisto swamp and Carolina bays
Bamberg County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums move out of the Edisto blackwater swamps into Bamberg and Denmark, armadillos root the sandy farm-edge lawns, and cottonmouths hold the swamp edges where yards meet wet ground
Bamberg County.absent_or_rare: groundhogs are uncommon in this flat Lowcountry county, and alligators in the Edisto backwaters are handled only through SCDNR's program

Barnwell County.region: the western Sandhills and Savannah River country below Aiken
Barnwell County.nearest_metro: Augusta, Georgia (about 45 miles west) and Aiken (about 25 miles north)
natural_features: the Savannah River and the Savannah River Site boundary
the Salkehatchie River headwaters
Lake Edgar Brown and the Sandhills longleaf tracts
Barnwell County.habitat_type: Sandhills longleaf and farm land falling west to Savannah River swamp, with creek bottoms through the center
Barnwell County.regional_wildlife: armadillos dig through the Sandhills sand in Barnwell and Blackville lawns, raccoons work the creek bottoms and river swamp, and moles ridge the sandy yards all season
Barnwell County.absent_or_rare: the southern hognose of the Sandhills is State Threatened and referral-only, and alligators in the river backwaters belong to SCDNR's program, not a private service list

Beaufort County.region: the Lowcountry sea islands and marsh coast between Charleston and Savannah
Beaufort County.nearest_metro: Hilton Head Island and Bluffton are the county's own growth centers; Savannah, Georgia is about 35 miles south
natural_features: the Beaufort River and Port Royal Sound
the sea-island marshes of St. Helena and Lady's Island
Hunting Island and the ACE Basin's southern edge
Beaufort County.habitat_type: sea islands, salt marsh, and live-oak maritime forest, with raised Lowcountry homes behind marsh and tidal creek
common_wildlife: marsh rabbits along the marsh edge
Beaufort County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums work the marsh and live-oak islands nightly, armadillos burrow the sandy island soils, Brazilian free-tailed bats roost in older Beaufort and Bluffton structures, and alligators hold the freshwater ponds behind the marsh
Beaufort County.absent_or_rare: alligators are never a listed service here — nuisance animals go to SCDNR's tag program and its contracted Alligator Control Agents — and groundhogs do not occur on the sea islands

Berkeley County.region: the inner Lowcountry around Lake Moultrie and the Cooper River, north of Charleston
natural_features: Lake Moultrie and the Cooper River
the Francis Marion National Forest's southern half
the Wando River and the county's blackwater creeks
Berkeley County.habitat_type: fast-growing Charleston suburbs against Lake Moultrie, national forest pine flatwoods, and Cooper River swamp
Berkeley County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels pour out of the Francis Marion forest edge into Goose Creek and Moncks Corner subdivisions, armadillos root the sandy new lawns, and lake-country homes take steady opossum and bat calls
Berkeley County.absent_or_rare: alligators in Lake Moultrie and the Cooper River are SCDNR-program animals only, and groundhogs are scarce on this flat coastal ground

Calhoun County.region: the central Midlands Sandhills between Columbia and Orangeburg, on the Congaree River
natural_features: the Congaree River floodplain
the Lake Marion upper shore and Santee swamp edge
the Sandhills farm country around St. Matthews
Calhoun County.habitat_type: Sandhills farms and pine land east of the Congaree River floodplain, with swamp hardwoods along the river and lake
Calhoun County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums come out of the Congaree floodplain into St. Matthews and Cameron, armadillos and moles work the deep Sandhills sand, and fox squirrels show in the open pine and pecan groves
Calhoun County.absent_or_rare: groundhogs are uncommon on this sandy flat ground, and alligators along the lake and river are referred to SCDNR's program

Charleston County.region: the central Lowcountry coast — the Charleston peninsula, sea islands, and marsh suburbs
Charleston County.nearest_metro: Charleston is itself the regional metro center
natural_features: Charleston Harbor and the Ashley and Cooper rivers
the Francis Marion National Forest's Wambaw swamp country
the sea-island marshes of Johns, James, and Wadmalaw islands
Charleston County.habitat_type: a tidal city and suburbs spread across peninsula, marsh islands, and river necks, with raised houses, crawlspaces, and live-oak canopy
Charleston County.regional_wildlife: Norway rats are a defining call in the peninsula's older blocks and food-service districts, raccoons work every marsh-edge neighborhood, roof-level squirrels and free-tailed bat colonies fill the older rooflines, and armadillos burrow island and suburban sand
Charleston County.absent_or_rare: alligators in the marsh ponds and golf lagoons go only to SCDNR's tag program and contracted agents, and groundhogs are absent from this coastal county's list

Cherokee County.region: the northern Upstate foothills on the North Carolina line, along the Broad River
Cherokee County.nearest_metro: Spartanburg (about 25 miles southeast) and Charlotte, North Carolina (about 55 miles northeast)
natural_features: the Broad River and its Kings Creek tributaries
the Cowpens battleground country and foothill hardwood ridges
Lake Wylie is east; the county's own waters are Broad River bottoms and farm ponds
Cherokee County.habitat_type: foothill mill towns and farmland in the Broad River valley, with hardwood ridges rising toward the North Carolina line
Cherokee County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow the foothill pastures and mill-town banks around Gaffney and Blacksburg, raccoons and skunks work the Broad River bottoms, and squirrels fill the older in-town canopy
Cherokee County.absent_or_rare: cottonmouths do not occur in this Upstate county, and copperheads in the rocky ridges are safety-and-identification calls only

Chester County.region: the north-central Piedmont on the Catawba and Broad rivers, between Charlotte and Columbia
Chester County.nearest_metro: Charlotte, North Carolina (about 45 miles north) and Columbia (about 55 miles south)
natural_features: the Catawba River and Fishing Creek
the Broad River's western bank
Landsford Canal and the county's Piedmont hardwood bottoms
Chester County.habitat_type: Piedmont mill towns, farmland, and hardwood river bottoms between the Catawba and Broad rivers
Chester County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs dig the pasture and railroad banks around Chester and Great Falls, raccoons follow Fishing Creek and the river bottoms into town, and armadillos have moved into the county's southern yards
Chester County.absent_or_rare: cottonmouths are not a Chester County snake, and alligator and diamondback copy has no place in this Piedmont county

Chesterfield County.region: the northeastern Sandhills on the North Carolina line, along the Great Pee Dee River
Chesterfield County.nearest_metro: Florence (about 40 miles southeast) and Charlotte, North Carolina (about 60 miles west)
natural_features: the Carolina Sandhills National Wildlife Refuge
the Great Pee Dee River and Lynches River
Lake Wallace and the county's longleaf sandhills
Chesterfield County.habitat_type: deep-sand longleaf Sandhills and refuge land west of the Great Pee Dee River swamps
Chesterfield County.regional_wildlife: fox squirrels run the open longleaf around Cheraw and the refuge, armadillos and moles work the deep sand, and raccoons commute the Pee Dee and Lynches river swamps into the farm towns
Chesterfield County.absent_or_rare: the southern hognose snake of these sandhills is State Threatened and referral-only, and the gopher tortoise reaches its Sandhills refuges here only as SCDNR referral content

Clarendon County.region: the central Lowcountry around Lake Marion's north shore
Clarendon County.nearest_metro: Sumter (about 25 miles north) and Charleston (about 80 miles southeast)
natural_features: Lake Marion, the state's largest lake
the Pocotaligo River swamp
the Black River headwater creeks and Wyboo swamp country
Clarendon County.habitat_type: flat farm and timber land wrapped around Lake Marion's swampy north shore and the Pocotaligo swamp
Clarendon County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums work the Lake Marion shoreline and Pocotaligo swamp into Manning and Summerton, armadillos root the sandy lake-edge lawns, and bat colonies hold the older in-town homes
Clarendon County.absent_or_rare: alligators in Lake Marion are SCDNR-program animals only, and groundhogs are scarce on this flat lake-plain ground

Colleton County.region: the western Lowcountry's ACE Basin — the Ashepoo, Combahee, and Edisto rivers
Colleton County.nearest_metro: Charleston (about 50 miles east) and Beaufort (about 35 miles south)
natural_features: the ACE Basin, one of the largest undeveloped estuaries on the East Coast
the Edisto River and its blackwater swamps
the Ashepoo and Combahee river marshes
Colleton County.habitat_type: ACE Basin marsh, blackwater river swamp, and pine flatwoods around small farm and rail towns
common_wildlife: feral hogs in the basin swamps
Colleton County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, opossums, and feral hogs move out of the ACE Basin swamps into Walterboro and the farm communities, armadillos root the flatwoods clearings, and bats hold Walterboro's older homes
Colleton County.absent_or_rare: alligators throughout the basin are SCDNR referral and tag-program content only, and groundhogs do not belong on this Lowcountry county's list

Darlington County.region: the western Pee Dee, between Florence and the Sandhills
natural_features: Black Creek and the Hartsville mill ponds
the Great Pee Dee River's western swamps
the Darlington raceway country and its farm fields
Darlington County.habitat_type: Pee Dee farm and mill-town land along Black Creek, with river swamp on the eastern edge
Darlington County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums follow Black Creek through Darlington and Hartsville, armadillos root the sandy farm-edge lawns, and skunks den under the older mill-town porches
Darlington County.absent_or_rare: groundhogs thin out sharply on this Pee Dee flat ground, and alligators in the river swamp are SCDNR-program referrals

Dillon County.region: the northern Pee Dee on the North Carolina line, along the Lumber and Little Pee Dee rivers
natural_features: the Little Pee Dee River and its swamps
the Lumber River bottoms
the county's tobacco-and-timber farm country
Dillon County.habitat_type: flat Pee Dee farm and timber land cut by the Little Pee Dee and Lumber river swamps
Dillon County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums commute the river swamps into Dillon and Latta, armadillos and moles work the sandy farm lawns, and skunks den under the older town housing
Dillon County.absent_or_rare: groundhogs are uncommon in this flat border county, and alligators in the river swamps belong to SCDNR's program

Dorchester County.region: the inner Lowcountry northwest of Charleston, along the Edisto and Ashley rivers
Dorchester County.nearest_metro: Charleston (about 30 miles southeast) and Summerville is the county's own growth center
natural_features: the Edisto River and Four Holes Swamp
the Ashley River's headwater swamps
Givhans Ferry and the county's pine flatwoods
Dorchester County.habitat_type: explosive Charleston suburban growth at Summerville against Edisto and Ashley river swamp and pine flatwoods
Dorchester County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels move out of the swamp and flatwoods into Summerville's canopy subdivisions, armadillos root the new sandy lawns, and opossums work the creek and swamp edges countywide
Dorchester County.absent_or_rare: alligators in the Edisto and the swamp ponds are SCDNR-program animals only, and groundhogs are not part of this Lowcountry county's fauna

Edgefield County.region: the western Piedmont on the Savannah River, in Sumter National Forest country
Edgefield County.nearest_metro: Augusta, Georgia (about 25 miles south) and Aiken (about 25 miles southeast)
natural_features: the Savannah River and Stevens Creek
Sumter National Forest's Long Cane country
the historic Edgefield pottery and town-square district
Edgefield County.habitat_type: Piedmont hardwood and pine ridges, national forest tracts, and farm valleys falling to the Savannah River
Edgefield County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow the pasture banks around Edgefield and Johnston, raccoons work Stevens Creek and the river bottoms, and bats hold colonies in the county's antebellum in-town homes
Edgefield County.absent_or_rare: cottonmouths stay in the Savannah River swamp fringe and are identification calls there, while alligators are absent from this county's working list

Fairfield County.region: the north-central Midlands Piedmont, between Columbia and the Catawba River
natural_features: Lake Wateree on the Catawba River
the Broad River's eastern bank
the Winnsboro granite quarries and rocky Piedmont ridges
Fairfield County.habitat_type: rocky Piedmont ridges, granite outcrops, and hardwood forest between the Broad and Catawba rivers, with Lake Wateree on the east
Fairfield County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow the rocky pasture banks around Winnsboro and Ridgeway, raccoons work both river corridors and the Wateree shore, and bats colonize the county's stone and antebellum in-town buildings
Fairfield County.absent_or_rare: cottonmouths and alligators have no place in this inland Piedmont county's copy, and copperheads among the granite outcrops are safety-and-identification content

Florence County.region: the central Pee Dee, at the crossing of I-95 and I-20
Florence County.nearest_metro: Florence is itself the regional center for the Pee Dee
natural_features: the Great Pee Dee River and Jeffries Creek
Lynches River on the western edge
the Florence rail yards and the county's farm and timber country
Florence County.habitat_type: a Pee Dee rail-and-interstate city ringed by farm and timber land, creek bottoms, and river swamp
Florence County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums follow Jeffries Creek through Florence's neighborhoods, Norway rats hold the older rail and commercial blocks, and armadillos root the county's sandy suburban lawns
Florence County.absent_or_rare: groundhogs are scarce on this flat Pee Dee ground, and alligators in the river swamps are referred to SCDNR's program

Georgetown County.region: the northern Lowcountry coast at Winyah Bay, between Charleston and Myrtle Beach
Georgetown County.nearest_metro: Myrtle Beach (about 35 miles north) and Charleston (about 60 miles south)
natural_features: Winyah Bay, where the Pee Dee, Waccamaw, Black, and Sampit rivers meet
the Waccamaw River and its cypress swamps
Brookgreen and the Murrells Inlet marsh creek country
Georgetown County.habitat_type: Winyah Bay marsh, barrier-island beaches, and cypress river swamp behind a coast of historic and resort communities
Georgetown County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums work the Waccamaw cypress swamps and marsh creeks into Georgetown, Pawleys, and Murrells Inlet, armadillos burrow the sandy island soils, and bats roost in the historic district's raised homes
Georgetown County.absent_or_rare: alligators in the bay, rivers, and golf ponds are SCDNR tag-program animals only — never a private removal service — and groundhogs are absent from the coast

Greenville County.region: the Upstate foothills at the Blue Ridge escarpment, the state's most populous county
Greenville County.nearest_metro: Greenville is itself the regional metro center
natural_features: the Reedy River and Falls Park in downtown Greenville
Paris Mountain and the Blue Ridge foothill ridges
the Saluda and Enoree river corridors
Greenville County.habitat_type: a foothill metro of dense suburbs and mill towns rising northwest to Paris Mountain and the Blue Ridge escarpment
Greenville County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow foothill banks and large-lot edges from Travelers Rest to Fountain Inn, squirrels and raccoons work the heavy canopy over Greenville's older neighborhoods, and bats colonize the mill-era and mountain-side homes
Greenville County.absent_or_rare: cottonmouths do not occur in this Upstate county, the mountain form of the timber rattlesnake in the far northern ridges is rare safety-and-referral content, and armadillos are still only an arriving southern-edge call

Greenwood County.region: the west-central Piedmont on Lake Greenwood and the Saluda River
Greenwood County.nearest_metro: Greenville (about 55 miles north) and Augusta, Georgia (about 60 miles southwest)
natural_features: Lake Greenwood on the Saluda River
the Saluda and Reedy river bottoms
Ninety Six and the county's Piedmont hardwood ridges
Greenwood County.habitat_type: Piedmont mill city and small towns ringed by farmland, hardwood ridges, and the Lake Greenwood shore
Greenwood County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow pasture and subdivision banks around Greenwood and Ninety Six, raccoons work the Saluda bottoms and lake shore, and armadillos have spread across the county's southern lawns
Greenwood County.absent_or_rare: cottonmouths are confined to the Saluda swamp fringe as identification calls, and alligator copy does not belong in this Piedmont county

Hampton County.region: the western Lowcountry between the Savannah and Salkehatchie rivers
Hampton County.nearest_metro: Beaufort (about 40 miles southeast) and Savannah, Georgia (about 55 miles southwest)
natural_features: the Salkehatchie River and its swamps
Lake Warren and the county's creek bottoms
the Coosawhatchie River headwaters
Hampton County.habitat_type: flat Lowcountry farm and timber land threaded by Salkehatchie and Coosawhatchie blackwater swamp
Hampton County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, opossums, and feral hogs move out of the Salkehatchie swamps into Hampton and Estill, armadillos root the sandy yards, and bats hold the older in-town homes
Hampton County.absent_or_rare: alligators in the river backwaters are SCDNR-program referrals only, and groundhogs are not a Hampton County animal

Horry County.region: the northern Lowcountry coast — the Grand Strand — on the Waccamaw River and the North Carolina line
Horry County.nearest_metro: Myrtle Beach is the county's own coastal center; Wilmington, North Carolina is about 75 miles north
natural_features: the Waccamaw River and its cypress swamps
the Grand Strand beaches from Little River to Garden City
Lewis Ocean Bay and the county's Carolina bays
Horry County.habitat_type: a booming coastal county of beach resorts, golf subdivisions, and Waccamaw cypress swamp behind the Strand
common_wildlife: Norway rats in the resort corridors
Horry County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums work the Waccamaw swamps and marsh creeks into every Strand community, armadillos burrow the sandy subdivision soils, Norway rats hold the resort and restaurant corridors, and bats roost in older Conway and beach homes
Horry County.absent_or_rare: alligators in the river, swamps, and golf-course ponds go only to SCDNR's tag program and contracted agents, and groundhogs are absent from this coastal county

Jasper County.region: the southern Lowcountry on the Savannah River, between Beaufort and Savannah
Jasper County.nearest_metro: Savannah, Georgia (about 30 miles south) and Hilton Head Island (about 25 miles east)
natural_features: the Savannah River and its refuge swamps
the Coosawhatchie and Tullifinny river marshes
the I-95 corridor's pine flatwoods and new subdivisions
Jasper County.habitat_type: Savannah River swamp, salt marsh creeks, and pine flatwoods carrying fast I-95 and Sun City growth
common_wildlife: feral hogs in the river swamp
Jasper County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, opossums, and feral hogs move out of the Savannah River swamp into Ridgeland and Hardeeville, armadillos root the new subdivision lawns, and marsh-edge homes take steady skunk and bat calls
Jasper County.absent_or_rare: alligators throughout the river and marsh ponds are SCDNR-program animals only, and groundhogs do not occur in this southern Lowcountry county

Kershaw County.region: the north-central Midlands Sandhills on the Wateree River
natural_features: the Wateree River and Lake Wateree's southern shore
the Lynches River headwaters
Camden's antebellum and horse-country estates
Kershaw County.habitat_type: Sandhills horse country and pine woods west of the Wateree River swamps, with Columbia suburbs at Lugoff and Elgin
Kershaw County.regional_wildlife: fox squirrels run Camden's open pine and horse country, raccoons work the Wateree swamps into Lugoff and Elgin, and armadillos dig the deep Sandhills sand across the county
Kershaw County.absent_or_rare: groundhogs reach only the county's northwestern Piedmont fringe as an occasional call, and the southern hognose of the sandhills is State Threatened and referral-only

Lancaster County.region: the north-central Piedmont on the Catawba River, in Charlotte's southern growth path
natural_features: the Catawba River and Lake Wylie is north; the county's waters are the Catawba and Lynches headwaters
Forty Acre Rock and the county's granite outcrops
the Andrew Jackson State Park pine and hardwood country
Lancaster County.habitat_type: Piedmont farmland and hardwood ridges north, exploding Charlotte suburbs at Indian Land in the panhandle
Lancaster County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow the Piedmont pastures around Lancaster and Kershaw, raccoons follow the Catawba bottoms, and Indian Land's new subdivisions take heavy squirrel, raccoon, and skunk calls against their wooded edges
Lancaster County.absent_or_rare: cottonmouths are not a Lancaster County snake, and copperheads around Forty Acre Rock and the granite ridges are safety-and-identification calls

Laurens County.region: the west-central Piedmont between Greenville and Columbia, on the Enoree and Saluda rivers
natural_features: the Enoree River and its Sumter National Forest tracts
the Saluda River's upper reaches
Lake Greenwood's northern coves
Laurens County.habitat_type: Piedmont mill towns, farmland, and national forest tracts between the Enoree and Saluda rivers
Laurens County.regional_wildlife: groundhogs burrow pasture banks across the county, raccoons work the Enoree forest corridor into Laurens and Clinton, and armadillos have spread into the southern lawns and farm edges
Laurens County.absent_or_rare: cottonmouths hold only the Saluda swamp fringe as identification calls, and timber rattlesnake copy does not belong in this Piedmont county

Lee County.region: the east-central Midlands between Sumter and Florence, on the Lynches River
Lee County.nearest_metro: Sumter (about 25 miles southwest) and Florence (about 35 miles east)
natural_features: the Lynches River and its swamps
Lee State Park's sandhills and artesian wells
the county's farm fields and pine stands
Lee County.habitat_type: flat farm and sandhills land cut by the Lynches River swamp, in the Pee Dee's western fringe
Lee County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and opossums commute the Lynches swamp into Bishopville, armadillos and moles work the sandy farm lawns, and skunks den under the older town and farm housing
Lee County.absent_or_rare: groundhogs are uncommon on this flat ground, and alligators in the river swamp are SCDNR-program referrals

Lexington County.region: the west-central Midlands on Lake Murray and the Saluda River, across from Columbia
Lexington County.nearest_metro: Columbia (directly across the Congaree and Saluda rivers)
natural_features: Lake Murray and its many residential coves
the Saluda River and Saluda Dam
Twelve Mile Creek and the county's pine and hardwood suburbs
Lexington County.habitat_type: Columbia's western suburbs and lake country around Lake Murray, with farm and pine land in the south and west
Lexington County.regional_wildlife: raccoons and squirrels work the Lake Murray shoreline canopy into Lexington, Irmo, and Chapin homes, armadillos root lawns across the county's sandy south, and bats hold colonies in the older West Columbia and Cayce housing
Lexington County.absent_or_rare: groundhogs reach only the county's far northwestern fringe as a rare call, and alligators are not part of Lake Murray's working list — a Murray alligator report goes to SCDNR

McCormick County.nearest_metro: Augusta, Georgia (about 55 miles southeast) and Greenwood (about 30 miles northeast)
natural_features: Lake Thurmond (Clarks Hill Lake) on the Savannah River
Sumter National Forest tracts across the county
Little River and the county's Piedmont creek bottoms
McCormick County.habitat_type: the state's second-least-populated county: national forest, lake shore, and farm valleys on the Savannah River
McCormick County.regional_wildlife: raccoons work the Thurmond shoreline and creek bottoms into McCormick and the lake communities, groundhogs burrow the farm banks, and bats hold the older in-town and camp-meeting housing
